controls_available.effect: Starts the autonomous beat phase; it is disabled after starting.
One on-beat click can move, attack, or wait; the first such click spends the beat.

controls_available.reason: The simplified browser handler ignores keyboard input.

controls_available.effect: Administrative certification of the recorded transcript.

autonomous_processes.period: After the clock starts and before terminal or exhaustion
autonomous_processes.process: Virtual task time and the visible beat pulse advance continuously; the browser resynchronizes the state every 50 ms.

Alive sentries act in order, the beat counter increments, and the one-action-per-beat lock resets. Crawlers and active hoppers chase or collide with the player; active lancers strike adjacent tiles while rooted.
The first 1150 ms is the gold action window. During the remaining 650 ms, visible button clicks are logged as off-beat and have no task-state effect; sentries still act at the next boundary.

autonomous_processes.period: After player death, escape, or 100 beats
autonomous_processes.process: Outcome-affecting progression stops; submission can still be attempted.

grouped_control_modes.name: simplified_direction_buttons
grouped_control_modes.scope: All on-beat direction-button occurrences across seeds and beats.

clause_i.reason: No observation-free q can choose an optimal button from I_t alone across this grouped mode. The L5 generator varies walls, start and exit positions, enemy positions, and per-enemy phase offsets by seed, while I_t contains only the agent's prior actions and times. Histories with the same I_t can therefore require different geometry- or phase-dependent directions, such as attacking a currently adjacent resting hopper versus evading a different visible threat.

clause_ii.reason: A 300 ms window (three configured frames) contains the visible board, walls, player and health, enemy positions and HP, roster phase telegraphs, hopper shield state, lancer danger tiles, and beat progress. These visible values determine the deterministic one-beat advance and let a bounded-window policy simulate the state at t+1800 ms and choose the corresponding direction button. The latest frame alone is sufficient; no unbounded memory or hidden seed is needed.

clause_iii.reason: Use the same direction-button mode with t about 300 ms into a gold window and Delta=1800 ms. In a reachable state with a hopper adjacent to the player and hopper phase 0 (REST / OPEN), the direction into it is available and returns hit, reducing its HP. If no action is supplied, at tau=1500 ms the autonomous beat boundary advances the beat; the hopper remains adjacent but is now phase 1 (SHIELD + CHASE), so the same direction button returns shield and does not reduce HP. A continuation remains possible, while the action's value or advantage over no-op has strictly fallen because of the hopper's non-clock state transition, not because the gold bar closed.

common_visible_process: The shared 1800 ms beat visibly advances the pulse and sentry phase telegraphs; at its boundary the sentries act and the next beat exposes changed positions, danger, or shield state. In the common hopper witness, REST / OPEN changes to SHIELD + CHASE, causing the same visible direction attack to lose effectiveness during the delay.

pre_run.reason: At difficulty 5 every generated board has four enemies with positive HP and an exit at Manhattan distance at least three from the start. After Wind the clock, a pre-run with no outcome-affecting actions can only let advance move or strike enemies; it never moves the player or reduces enemy HP. The win flag is set only by act after the player moves to the exit with all enemies defeated. Thus no generated instance admits a successful no-action autonomous phase, so the 50% threshold is not met; no percentage is asserted.

source_evidence.claim: The exact L5 profile is a 9x9 board with 9 walls, crawler/hopper/two-lancer enemies, enemy health 2, and player health 2; simplified mode is click direction and wait buttons; the configured observation window is 300 ms with three frames.
The runner supplies a 180-second play allowance, 300 ms observation windows, three frames, and mouse/keyboard device types.

The control condition overrides the profile, seeded generation randomizes connected walls, start/exit, enemy positions and phase offsets, and the generated board sets beat_ms=1800, open_ms=1150, max_beats=100 while preserving the control condition in public and truth state.

The browser selects simplified versus full interaction from control_condition; act permits one action, blocks a hopper in phase 1, changes enemy HP on attack, moves the player, and sets win only at the cleared exit.
sync advances the state at each elapsed 1800 ms boundary; crawlers and active hoppers chase or damage, phase-1 lancers strike adjacent tiles, and each beat resets the action lock.
The visible UI shows the gold/listen beat state, roster phase transitions, hopper shield styling, lancer danger tiles, and only direction buttons for simplified mode; off-beat clicks do not call act.
The pulse bar visibly presents the gold portion of the beat and the board/roster styling exposes the player, enemies, shield, and danger state.
The independent replay uses the same initial state, phase function, attack rules, enemy advance rules, and beat reset, including hopper shield and rooted lancer behavior.

The grader requires the simplified direction_buttons source, validates event times against the 1800/1150 beat, replays autonomous boundaries, and passes only when the replay reaches the cleared exit with matching final state.

The provided planner treats wall, unavailable, and shield outcomes as unusable and searches action-plus-autonomous-advance routes, confirming that successful continuation depends on the changing tactical state; it is implementation evidence rather than policy information.
Verification loads the exported result and invokes the independent clockbeat grader rather than trusting client state.
The shared controller gives timers and performance.now a virtual task clock and separates it from native wall time, so the mechanic's elapsed-time loop is the task-time process.
The shared live/paused controller freezes virtual task time, drains task timers only while running, and advances the same task-time timers/animation callbacks when a window is run.
The wiring solver starts the clock and sends exactly one planned input per beat while checking the visible beat and timing; its private public_state access is not used as policy evidence.
